agentSignupMetadata.description:
Read API-key record metadata associated with current account emails matching the case-insensitive agent+ prefix. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential for a Recoup admin account. Admin access is checked before query validation or metadata access.

Each returned record contains only id, name, email and created_at. id identifies an API-key record, not an account or credential; no API key value or hash is selected or returned. email is the first matching current associated email, not necessarily a primary or canonical address. Multiple matching emails do not multiply a key record; multiple keys on one account remain separate records. Deleted keys are absent; expired key records are not excluded. Current email associations can change. This is a current-email metadata selection, not evidence of origin from POST /api/agents/signup, a unique-agent/account count, active-key count, usage or adoption.

period defaults to all. Other values use inclusive midnight-UTC calendar boundaries on API-key record created_at: daily is today; weekly includes today and the preceding six calendar days; monthly includes today and the preceding 29 calendar days. Rows are ordered by key-record created_at descending. total is the length of the returned signups array, not a separate database-wide count. Existing database visibility and server row limits apply; no pagination or collection-completeness guarantee is provided. A successful empty read returns total 0 and signups []; a read failure returns a masked 500 instead.

This is GET /api/admins/agent-signups. The former GET /api/admins/agent/signups remains unavailable. The broader reporting decision in Mono #327 and original API #428 are not closed by this metadata route. Source tests use synthetic credential and storage boundaries; they do not prove production admin access, real data completeness or customer adoption. No UI, automatic caller, polling job, export or account/key creation is added.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Optional key-record creation window, inclusive from 00:00 UTC: daily = today; weekly = 7 calendar days including today; monthly = 30 calendar days including today; all = no cutoff. Defaults to all when omitted; an explicit empty or unsupported value returns 400. This is not a rolling 24-hour window and does not filter by account or email creation time.

total.description: Number of key records in this returned signups array. Not a separate database-wide count or a count of unique accounts, agents, active keys or adoption.

signups.description: Returned metadata rows ordered by key-record created_at descending. The retained wire name does not establish signup origin. Multiple keys for one account remain separate rows.

parameters.name: streamLifecycle
parameters.description: Send streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1 exactly once on the initial POST and every reconnect GET to keep server work running when that reader disconnects. Only exactly one parameter with that exact value opts in. Omitting it, an empty or unknown value, or repeating the parameter retains legacy disconnect cancellation. Use authenticated POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop for cancellation; a local reader abort is not confirmation that server work stopped. This is a query parameter, not a request-body field.

parameters.name: chatId
parameters.description: UUID of the chat to resume.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Act on a chat belonging to another account. Only honoured for a key that is authorised for that account — an organization key may pass a member account's id; a personal key passing anyone else's is rejected with `403 Access denied to specified account_id`. Omit it to act as the authenticated account.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
Zero-based index of the first stream chunk to return, so a client that was already receiving this response resumes where it left off instead of replaying the whole turn.

Pass the number of chunks already received. Omit it to receive the response from the beginning — the right choice for a fresh reader such as a page load, or a client watching a headless [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) run for the first time.

A long turn's stream can end before the run does; reconnecting with `startIndex` is how a client keeps rendering without duplicating or skipping chunks.
